cultural.vision_reason: A multi-strip narrow-loom cotton cloth with complex warp stripes and weft-faced supplementary blocks, a classic Ewe kente-type man's wrap cloth from Ghana, matching the claimed ethnicity and category.

physical.title: textile
physical.summary: Ewe cloth; man's wrap-around garment with cotton warp and weft. Composed of 21 narrow strips handsewn together in black cotton, selvedge to selvedge. Each strip consists of repeating plain weave warp stripes in same combination of black-, blue-, white-, red-, green-, yellow-, and cream-dyed cotton. Each warp strip includes a 'tweed' effect stripe formed by twisting together yellow and blue threads into a single strand. Warp stripes alternate at fixed intervals with weft-faced blocks in red-, yellow-, pink-, white-, blue- and purple-dyed cotton. Discontinuous suppplementary weft motifs are interspersed between the warp stripes and weft blocks and include motifs such as animals, birds and human figures as well as fans, hearts, trees, tools and combs. The cloth has turned and hand-stitched hems at either end.
